neighbours.label: vocabulary of social-inclusion and civil-rights discourse (accommodation, 'coming out', second-wave feminism, competitive employment for people with disabilities); the other side of the + pole's intrinsic worth / dignity
fire: The office installed ramps as a reasonable accommodation for employees who use wheelchairs.
Many teenagers find coming out to their parents the hardest step of all.
The second wave of feminism pushed for equal pay and reproductive rights.
The program helps adults with disabilities find competitive employment in their towns.
She asked her classmates to stop making inconsiderate jokes about autism.
The charity campaigns for the inclusion of deaf students in ordinary schools.
Activists marched to demand equal rights for gay and lesbian couples.
The workshop taught managers how to support neurodivergent staff.
quiet: The office installed new printers on every floor for the employees.
Many teenagers find learning to drive the hardest step of all.
The second wave of the flu reached the city in early spring.
The program helps adults find affordable housing in their towns.
She asked her classmates to stop making noise during the exam.
The charity campaigns for the planting of trees in ordinary schools.
Farmers marched to demand higher prices for milk and grain.
The workshop taught managers how to prepare quarterly budgets.

notes: Card: weak pole (max 5.6), no single token: 'second wave' feminism, 'coming out', accommodation, inconsiderate about autism, competitive employment for disabilities. The + pole fires on worth/dignity of every individual. Near misses keep an institutional/social register without the inclusion theme.
